observation_summary: The method NumberUtils.createNumber throws a NumberFormatException when parsing single-digit long literals like '1l' because the logic incorrectly requires at least one digit after the first character.
reasoning_summary: The bug is caused by an overly restrictive conditional check in the code. The original logic used 'isDigits(numeric.substring(1))', which fails for single-digit numbers because the substring is empty. The fix modifies this conditional predicate to correctly handle both negative numbers (requiring digits after the sign) and positive single-digit numbers (allowing the entire string to be digits). This is a classic predicate logic error.
evidence_used: The bug report states: 'The condition isDigits(numeric.substring(1)), line 455 return false as numeric.substring(1) is an empty string for "1l"'
The fix diff modifies the conditional expression in the 'case 'L'' block to correctly validate the input string structure.
